results.rationale: Consistency: a dark framed board overlays the original wooden grid, and most stone colors, numbers and placements change. Instruction: instead of adding one black stone immediately left of the original four-stone row, the edit replaces the game with many new stones and a different arrangement. Knowledge: this does not represent the required legal single-stone winning move; instruction failure ⇒ knowledge invalid. Quality: the new board frame and glossy stones are structurally coherent and cleanly rendered.

Consistency: the desert foreground, distant skyline, blue sky and illumination remain consistent outside the pyramid replacement. Instruction: broad stepped terraces and central stairways are added, conveying a Maya-style pyramid, but the pointed cap lacks the expected flat-topped summit temple. Knowledge: the structure does not accurately match the specified Kukulkan Pyramid because of that conspicuous summit mismatch. Quality: the stone terraces, stairways and shadows are coherent and naturally integrated into the scene.
